title: Local404: Do AI assistants say closed neighborhood restaurants in Korea are still open? (800 restaurants, 5 languages, 4 response systems)
description: Define404 Research preregistration. Full Korean protocol: prereg.md (canonical). Author: Hawon Kim (Define404).

responses.78-2: It's complicated. We have already collected some data but explain in Question 8 why readers may consider this a valid pre-registration nevertheless.
responses.78-7:
H1 (primary): Among closed restaurants, the share of answers that assert the restaurant is open is higher than, among open restaurants, the share of answers that assert it is closed.
H2: Accuracy of the business-status answer is lower for non-Korean questions (English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Vietnamese) than for the same restaurant asked in Korean.
H3: The error rate (asserting the wrong status) of Claude Haiku with web search is lower than Claude Haiku without tools, compared on the same restaurant and language.
H4: Among closed restaurants, the probability of an 'open' assertion decreases as time since closure increases.
H5: For some restaurants the same system gives inconsistent status judgments across the five languages; we estimate this inconsistency rate (reported separately from accuracy) and expect it to be greater than zero.
responses.78-9: Each answer is coded for business status as one of: asserts open / asserts closed / unknown (cannot confirm). Ground truth: business status in the Korean local government licensing dataset (general restaurants, file.localdata.go.kr, downloaded 2026-10-21, SHA256 2b548c6e...ab24b4, 2,305,461 rows). Secondary variables: address correct (same eup/myeon/dong or road name), cuisine category correct (8 groups). Lenient scoring = status only; strict scoring = every stated item (status, address, category) correct. Automatic coding rules will be frozen in judge/rules.md before main collection; a random 200 answers are double-coded by two humans independently and we report percent agreement and Cohen's kappa.
responses.78-11: Restaurants: 2 (open vs closed, per licensing data) x 2 (listed vs not listed on Kakao Map) x 2 (metropolitan city vs province), 100 restaurants per cell, 800 total. Each restaurant is asked one question (is it still open, its address, and what kind of restaurant) in 5 languages using fixed templates (question_templates.json v1.1; names and districts kept in Korean script). Response systems: S-search = Claude Sonnet 5.5 with web search; H-search = Claude Haiku 5.5 with web search; H-mem = Claude Haiku 5.5 without tools; W-mem = Cloudflare Workers AI @cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fp8-fast without tools (max 300 output tokens). Claude systems are run as sub-agents that receive only the questions (one language per batch, at most 50 different restaurants per batch, order shuffled by fixed seed); they are not told the study purpose or ground truth.
responses.78-13: Primary (H1): difference between P(asserts open | closed) and P(asserts closed | open), per system, with 95% CIs using restaurant-clustered standard errors. H2: per-language accuracy and paired differences vs Korean for the same restaurant. H3: paired difference H-search vs H-mem on the same restaurant and language. H4: mixed-effects logistic regression on closed restaurants: asserts-open ~ log(days since closure) + (1 | restaurant). H5: share of restaurants whose five-language status judgments are not all identical, per system, with 95% CI. Overall model: correct ~ language + status + Kakao listing + region + system + (1 | restaurant). Holm correction across H1-H5. Cells with fewer than 40 observations are not interpreted. All other analyses are labeled exploratory.
responses.78-15: Restaurants excluded before sampling: missing address, name shorter than 2 characters, the same name appearing 2+ times within the same district, closed without a closure date. Answers that remain empty after up to 2 retries are treated as missing and their rate is reported. If coding rules change after main collection, results under the original rules are also reported.
responses.78-17: 800 restaurants (400 open, 400 closed), each asked in 5 languages to 4 systems (16,000 answers). Rationale: detecting a 10 percentage-point difference for H1 at alpha 0.05 and 80% power with worst-case proportion 0.5 requires about 392 per group. Sample drawn with seed 20261021 (sample_v2.csv, SHA256 4aaf1ecd...bc24871, code draw_sample_v2.py).
responses.78-19: Data already collected (Q1): (a) the public licensing dataset used as ground truth and for sampling; (b) a pilot of 80 answers (4 restaurants x 5 languages x 4 Claude conditions) used only to check format and tool restriction. In the pilot all 80 answers were 'cannot confirm' because randomly drawn restaurants have almost no web presence; this floor effect led us to add the Kakao Map listing stratum. Pilot answers are excluded from all analyses. No main-study answers have been collected. Limitations noted in advance: only freely accessible systems are included (paid AI search products excluded); batch context effects within a sub-agent; Kakao listing is only a proxy for online visibility; licensing data lags reality by about 2 days. Conflict of interest: the author runs Define404, which may offer AI-visibility diagnostics to small businesses; no Define404 product is tested.
responses.78-21: Local404: AI answers about closed neighborhood restaurants in Korea
